Both approaches aim to generate lines that enhance the perception of form, with the choice between them dictated by the availability of analytical data and performance constraints [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that analytical and pixel-based approaches fall into two categories optimized for different circumstances. It notes that analytical approaches require 'explicit analytical representations' (implying the availability of analytical data), while pixel-based methods are used 'when explicit analytical representations of models are not readily available' and are 'faster and simpler to implement' (implying performance constraints). Furthermore, the text mentions that lines in principal directions 'communicate surface shape better,' supporting the claim that the approaches aim to enhance the perception of form.
